title: FADD is recruited to activated STING oligomers initiating caspase mediated NF-κB activation in Drosophila melanogaster
projectDescription: STING is an evolutionarily conserved key regulator of innate immunity. In mammals, STING activates two distinct signaling pathways, the IRF3 and the NF-κB pathways, which act in conjunction to drive antiviral immunity. While the molecular mechanism of STING-mediated IRF3 activation has been untangled by extensive work during the last decade, how STING activates NF-κB signaling remains poorly understood. The versatile FADD/Caspase 8 axis is widely used in various immune signaling pathways throughout the animal kingdom and here we show that this axis participates downstream of STING in the activation of the Drosophila NF-kB like transcription factor Relish. We provide a detailed structural model illustrating how FADD interacts with two separate STING dimers in the activated oligomerized form of STING, thus providing a molecular explanation for the signal-dependent recruitment of FADD. In the classic IMD signaling pathway, FADD interacts with IMD in a structural distinct but functional related manner, highlighting how the two pathways differentially utilize the adapter FADD.
sampleProcessingProtocol: For IP/MS S2 cells were seeded in 6-well plates (3 x 106 cells/well, 4 wells/conditions, 2.5 mL/well). After 24 h the cells were transfected with DNA encoding V5-tagged Sting (17.5 µg/well), and cGAS (7.5 µg/well) or empty plasmid (7.5 µg/well) using JetOptimus® transfection reagent (PolyPlus). A control condition with DNA encoding EGFP (25.0 µg/well) was included. Cells were harvested 24 h after transfection, washed once with ice-cold phosphate-buffered saline (1× PBS), and resuspended in 1 mL NET buffer (50 mM Tris HCl [pH 7.4], 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1% dodecyl-β-D-maltoside (DDM), 10 µM iodoacetamide (IAA), 10% glycerol) and supplemented with 1x cOmplete™, EDTA-free Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (5056489001, Roche). Cells were lysed by 30 mins. rotation (2 rpm) at 4°C followed by 3x30 s sonication (Fisherbrand™ Elmasonic Select 30, ThermoScientific). The lysates were cleared by 15 min centrifugation at 17.000 g, 4°C. 100 µL Anti-V5 Agarose Affinity Gel antibody (A7345, SigmaAldrich) was added to each sample, and the volume was adjusted to 2 mL with NET buffer. Samples were rotated for 4 hours (2 rpm) at 4°C to allow immunoprecipitation. The beads were washed four times with 1 mL of NET buffer before bound proteins were eluted with 200 μL 100 mM glycin buffer (pH 2.5) at RT for 10 mins. Samples were prepared for mass spectrometry by the filter-aided sample preparation method as described elsewhere (Wisniewski et al, 2009). The samples were analysed on an Orbitrap Eclipse Tribrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an EASY 1200 nLC (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were loaded onto a trap column (2 cm x 75 µm i.d.) and separated on an analytical column (20 cm x 75 µm i.d.) packed with 1.9 µm C18 beads (Dr. Maisch, GmbH). The samples were eluted at a flow rate of 250 nl/min and with a gradient from 5 to 35 % acetonitrile for either 50 min or 80 min followed by a steep increase to 80 % acetonitrile for 10 min.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files were processed in Proteome Discoverer 2.5 using the Sequest HT search algorithm. The UniProt D. melanogaster reference proteome (v2023-06-28) was used as a database and the following search parameters: 10 ppm precursor mass accuracy, 0.02 Da fragment mass accuracy, trypsin as digestion enzyme, max. 2 missed cleavage sites, Oxidation (M) as dynamic modification and Acetyl (N-term), Met-loss (M), and Met-loss+Acetyl (M) as dynamic protein N-terminus modifications. Carbamidomethyl (C) as static modification. Protein abundances were label-free quantified based on precursor area and on unique peptides. Data was filtered to only include proteins identified with a 1 % FDR.
